committee: CC City Council Meeting of the Whole
overview: The Medford City Council Committee of the Whole serves as a deliberative body for all city councilors to conduct detailed reviews of municipal budgets, legislative proposals, infrastructure projects, and city staffing. Across 75 meetings held from June 2023 through October 2026, the committee carried out extensive preliminary departmental budget hearings each spring and developed specialized local ordinances. Its primary responsibilities include evaluating multi-year planning and zoning updates, Community Preservation Act allocations, and Community Development Block Grant action plans. In its most recent meetings, the body advanced a consultant procurement for the next phase of citywide zoning updates and conducted executive sessions on pending municipal litigation.

threads.name: Annual budget hearings and fiscal planning
threads.summary: Each spring, the committee conducts preliminary departmental hearings to evaluate general fund requests, enterprise fund balances, and administrative staffing. The body systematically compiles individual and collective council priorities for submission to the mayor while addressing recurring structural deficits and the sunsetting of federal ARPA and ESSER funds. Following the passage of Proposition 2 1/2 overrides, the review process for fiscal years 2026 and 2027 focused heavily on settled collective bargaining agreements, rising health insurance, and school department deficits. At its latest budget hearing, Mayor Lungo-Koehn presented the proposed $218.2 million general fund and $30.0 million water and sewer operating budgets for FY 2027.

threads.name: Zoning reform and commercial planning
threads.summary: The committee oversees major updates to the city's zoning code and economic development frameworks in conjunction with planning staff and outside consultants. In 2023, the body evaluated a multi-family overlay district at Wellington Station to satisfy the MBTA Communities Act and approved hiring Innes Associates for comprehensive zoning recodification. Subsequent sessions reviewed a 99-year lease redevelopment proposal for Medford Square parking lots and findings from the Wellington Transformation Study. Most recently, the committee voted to advance a new Request for Proposals for a zoning consultant to lead the next multi-year phase of citywide zoning updates.

threads.name: Tree protection and preservation ordinances
threads.summary: Efforts to protect and expand the municipal tree canopy involved extensive drafting across three interconnected ordinance proposals. In October 2023, the committee reviewed private property tree regulations and amended the structure of a proposed Tree Committee before referring the matters for departmental review. The regulations were separated into public and private components in November 2024, resulting in the referral of an amended Tree Committee ordinance to the full council in July 2025. In July 2026, the committee adopted amendments modifying resident notice requirements for sidewalk tree removals and referred the public tree ordinance to the regular council meeting.

threads.name: Leaf blower regulations
threads.summary: Under Paper 21-057, the committee considered draft ordinances to regulate noise, seasonal usage, and commercial operation of leaf blowers. In November 2023, the committee adopted eleven amendments to align hours with the noise ordinance, permit electric blowers year-round, and restrict seasonal gas-powered blowers. The committee debated further language adjustments addressing public feedback on operational and environmental impacts in February 2024, subsequently voting to report the ordinance out of committee as amended.

threads.name: Standard compensation and contracted labor standards
threads.summary: Beginning in early 2026, the committee considered an amendment to the standard compensation ordinance establishing a wage and benefit floor for contracted service workers such as janitorial and security staff. The matter was initially tabled and held in committee to evaluate legal viability and procurement impacts. In April 2026, councilors debated revisions addressing labor peace, worker retention, and administrative policies governing access to legal counsel, ultimately voting to report the redlined ordinance to the regular meeting.

threads.name: Community Preservation Act funding
threads.summary: The committee annually evaluates project recommendations submitted by the Community Preservation Committee for open space, historic preservation, and affordable housing. In February 2024, the committee recommended approval of ten FY 2024 projects totaling over $1.1 million, followed by an $1.8 million funding round for eight FY 2025 projects that was forwarded to the council in January 2025. In January 2026, the committee voted to favorably refer approximately $2.4 million across eleven FY 2026 projects, including allocations for the Medford Affordable Housing Trust and historic cemetery restoration.

threads.name: Community Development Block Grant action plans
threads.summary: Each spring, the committee holds formal reviews of the annual Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Action Plans, taking presentations from municipal staff and non-profit public service subrecipients. The committee reviewed and favorably referred a $1.38 million action plan for FY 2025 in May 2024 and an equivalent $1.384 million plan for FY 2026 in April 2025. In April 2026, the committee examined the Program Year 52 allocation of $1.433 million and referred the draft plan to the regular meeting for a final vote.

threads.name: Executive session litigation strategy
threads.summary: The committee periodically convenes in executive sessions closed to the public to establish legal strategies for active federal and state litigation. The body entered executive session in June 2025 regarding Aleesha Nunley Benjamin v. City of Medford, and again in March and April 2026 regarding Chertog v. City of Medford. Most recently, the committee voted to enter executive session in October 2026 to discuss strategy in Alua et al. v. City of Medford et al. before adjourning.
